en: The First Fascicle of the Chapter on the Great Maṇḍala of the Lotus of All Tathāgatas:
The Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva from the Teachings of the King of Dharma,
the Great Ritual Manual of Vajraśekhara Trailokyavijaya.

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Da Xingshan Monastery—Grand Master with the Rank of Kai-fu Yitong Sansi, Special Advancement, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Su Commandery with a Fief of Three Thousand Households, Recipient of the Purple Robe, Posthumously Honored as Minister of Works, and Entitled Dajian (Great Mirror), bearing the Title Dayangzhi (Great and Vast Wisdom)—by Imperial Decree. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, I wish to proclaim the mantra of my own mind within this assembly of the Dharma King of the Trailokyavijaya Ritual.
World-Honored One, if one merely utters the name of all Tathāgatas..."
When this samādhi manifests before one, all fears, calamities, obstacles,
and afflictions of illness shall be completely extinguished.
At that time, the Bhagavān...
He addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"Excellent, excellent! You should speak well.
Then the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara—
Receiving the Buddha’s holy command, he then spoke the mantra of his own heart, saying:
*Aruḷigaṃ saḥ svāhā*. As soon as this heart-mantra was spoken,
All the Tathāgatas, gathering from their original lands,
assembled at the summit of Mount Sumeru within the great assembly of Vairocana;
surrounding the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, they further proclaimed the great maṇḍala of the mantra of his own heart.
The courtyard layout is established by dividing the square;
within it, at the four corners and the four gates, the center is well-measured.
By laying out four lines in the shape of a well, eight positions are clearly formed, which are divided into an eight-petaled flower.
This form should be applied with vermilion;
in each of those petals, one should paint the image of the Great Awakened One.
In the central court, there shall be no door; inside and out, there are eight-lined paths.
Having thus established the subtle [mandala],
the ācārya should enter and respond within the maṇḍala; forming the great lotus mudrā,
with body upright and limbs composed, he should abide in samādhi.
Next, bind the Aṅkuśī mudrā and invite the Noble One.
If all sentient beings enter this maṇḍala, even while remaining at the level of ordinary persons,
their afflictions of greed and hatred and the stains of their transgressions shall be extinguished.
Just as a lotus flower is not defiled by water,
so too is the supreme birth not stained by desire.
Then the Ācārya [uses] the Great Lotus Mudrā.
Bending the forefinger with a force like a hook,
one should invoke Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
The mantra of the Lotus Hook is as follows:
Oṃ mahāpādma hūṃ jaḥ. At that moment, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara arrived at the site of practice, manifesting a subtle and wondrous form-body, or emitting rays of light.
The ācārya should next lead the disciples in according to the Dharma.
These disciples should wear white garments and further cover their clothing with white silk.
Furthermore, his head was bound with a clean cloth.
Once he had been led inside, a verse was spoken:
"Just as a lotus flower is not defiled by water,"
The Victorious Birth is likewise; without being defiled by any desires,
one should then place a lotus in the disciple’s left hand and a rosary in his right hand.
Furthermore, it is said in verse:
The great lotus of all Buddhas Is the foremost among all maṇḍalas;
One must always discern and contemplate it.
Having first personally worshipped Avalokiteśvara, one should then teach the mudrās and the gates of samādhi.
Regarding the Heart Mantra and the Lotus Maṇḍala Chapter: furthermore, as before, one should establish the maṇḍala.
The practitioner should sit upon the central platform and enter the *samādhi* of the blossoming lotus of all Tathāgatas.
By reciting one hundred thousand (*lakṣa*) times, one immediately attains the body of Avalokiteśvara.
Chapter on the Heart Mantra Samaya Maṇḍala: Furthermore, one should establish the maṇḍala as previously described.
One should take one thousand lotus flowers;
reciting the mantra once for each flower, place them in the central altar as an offering.
Thereafter, lead the disciple in and inform them of the samaya, which refers to the vow that all desires are pure.
The Chapter on the Karma Maṇḍala. Furthermore, having established the maṇḍala as previously described, one should perform the fourfold offerings.
Next, one should accomplish the method for forming the image.
Upon a clean silk cloth,
one should paint the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara seated upon the summit of Mount Sumeru, surrounded by the eight Buddhas.
Beginning on the first day of the waxing moon,
one should enter samādhi and perform recitation before this image at all times without interruption,
until the painted image emits light.
From within the light, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and all the Tathāgatas emerge;
they enter the practitioner’s brow, the site of consecration,
and remain there firmly established.
Immediately, the practitioner’s body becomes identical to that of Avalokiteśvara.
In a single instant, they behold the world of Sukhāvatī.
All sentient beings see them as they depart, their lifespan now immeasurable.
I shall now further explain the method for accomplishment:
by reciting one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*),
all obscurations and hindrances will be completely purified.
If one recites it two hundred thousand times,
all transgressions, including the five crimes of immediate retribution, will be extinguished without remainder.
If one recites it three hundred thousand times, [the same result follows].
All merits and virtues gather together;
all Tathāgatas are fully present;
all perfected wisdom manifests before one.
Furthermore, if one binds the Great Seal— that is, the accomplishment of the five signs—
and recites [the mantra] for one hundred thousand times (*lakṣa*) through the night without limit,
by the time of dawn, all Tathāgatas will enter the practitioner’s heart.
Their very essence is identical to that of the Tathāgata.
If they enter the mouth, their very essence becomes identical to that of Avalokiteśvara.
Furthermore, one accomplishes all activities.
Reciting it once protects one's own body;
twice protects others as well as cities, towns, and villages;
and three times enables the accomplishment of all undertakings.
If one performs the *avaśa* rite, one should burn sandalwood incense empowered by reciting the mantra eight hundred times and offer it as smoke into the fire-pit.
To pacify various malevolent spirits and demons, one should append the syllable *hili* and recite it.
To cause all sentient beings to become compliant:
empower a *vajra-flower* and substitute it with a red flower to render their evil intentions immovable.

Using white earth and the mantra for pacification, first write the name in vermilion at the head of the mantra, then roll it up and place it inside a flask. Fill it with white earth and bury it in a pit; afterwards, fill the pit with soil. Visualize Mount Sumeru situated there, and by doing so, one may even gain mastery over its upper and lower regions, causing the *siddhis* to be revered and drawn toward oneself.
By consecrating *sumana* flowers,
one causes them to submit and follow.
Furthermore, if one desires to cause all birds and beasts to remain motionless wherever they are, one should use white mustard seeds to render all birds and beasts unable to move.
Consecrate white mustard seeds and cast them from afar.
If one wishes to manifest a sign,
consecrate a peacock feather and wave it from afar.
If one wishes to know all matters within a dream,
one should recite [the mantra] three times that night and they will be seen.
Furthermore, if one wishes to eliminate bad dreams:
Perform homa with sesame seeds to [achieve one's aims].
Furthermore, if one wishes to silence the mouths of others, perform homa with the feathers from the wings of a rooster.
If one is a maiden, use *vāgīśvarī* [hair]; if a courtesan, use a menstrual cloth (*rajasvalāvastra*) for the homa.
*Svabhāṣikaraṇa*.
If one seeks any undertaking, one should extensively make offerings to Avalokiteśvara;
by fasting for one day and one night on the eighth day and reciting the mantra, all vows will be fulfilled.
Furthermore, if one recites this three times each during the three periods of the day before the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara for a full three months,
the Bodhisattva will fulfill all of one's aspirations.
Furthermore, before an image of the Buddha, recite this three times during each of the three periods of the day.
After three months have passed, the Buddha will fulfill one's wishes.

Regarding the mudrās in the Chapter on Mudrās: join the palms; interlace the two water fingers and the two wind fingers; place them upon the earth; and extend the space fingers upward, keeping them separate.
The joining of the two fire-fingers constitutes the Root Seal (*mūla-mudrā*).
The lotus-clasp (*padma-añjali*) is the Great Lotus Seal (*mahā-padma-mudrā*). One should not release the Great Lotus Seal;
with it opened, one should extend the fingers toward the earth and the sky.
This is the seal for averting and seizing all sins.
Furthermore, form the outer vajra-bind with the hands,
joining the two *vāyu* fingers like lotus petals.
The two empty hands pressed vertically against one another is the seal of samādhi.
Furthermore, separate the two hands to form lotus fists,
then rotate the wisdom fist around the concentration fist.
Forming the gesture of opening eight petals is the *karmamudrā*; it is for inviting the Tathāgata. Contemplate the syllable *hrīḥ* upon the moon-lotus of the heart;
this is the *dharmamudrā*.
Contemplate all phenomena as being like a lotus flower that is unstained by water.
All phenomena are likewise unstained by desire and the like;
this is the Seal of Wisdom (Jñānamudrā) of the Lotus Ācārya.
When intending to confer the rank of ācārya upon a disciple,
one places a lotus flower into the two palms of the disciple.
Furthermore, one consecrates the lotus garland one thousand and eight times.
Tie it upon the head of the disciple and perform the empowerment.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ padmamālābhiṣekalabdhīśvara-sūṣya. By this, one becomes an ācārya within the Lotus Family.
I shall now explain the ritual for the observance of the precepts for the practice of the Lotus Family (*padmakula*).
First, one should make offerings to the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and consume a handful of *gumutra* (cow urine), or at least a small portion of *māyi*.
Then all shall be purified.
One should then visualize oneself as the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara and recite this one thousand times daily for up to seven days.
The precepts will be accomplished.
From this point forward, whether eating all kinds of food or acting in all places,
one shall never be defiled.
I shall now explain the general ritual for all offerings:
form the vajra-fists with both hands and place them at the sides of the waist.
Bowing the head slightly to the left constitutes a respectful salutation. Then,
with both hands, move them from the forehead toward the back in the manner of binding a floral garland.
Passing through the successive *kalās* and hanging down the lower band—
this is the offering of a flower garland (*mālā*).
Furthermore, with both hands, one gradually moves upward from the navel to the mouth.
This is the offering of song and chant. Furthermore,

with both hands starting from the mouth, passing through the *tathāgata* and *prajñā* [mudrās], extending them, rotating them around each other, and finally joining the palms above the crown of the head,
this is the offering of the Vajra Dance.
By means of this offering, even the state of a Tathāgata is not difficult to attain,
let alone other siddhis. Why is this?
Because no bliss whatsoever is equal to that of this Vajrasattva.
From the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-mahākalparāja*, the Chapter on the Great Maṇḍala of the Lotus of All Tathāgatas, containing the Heart Mantra of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. One fascicle.
